clue.text: Personally choose worker with a digger

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a pick is a tool for digging

explanation.surface: A labourer is paired up with somebody to do the excavating.
explanation.definitionFit: To handpick is to select carefully and in person, rather than leaving the selection to others.

clue.text: Outburst of cheek cramping lecturer?

indicators.note: cramping means the scrambled letters squeeze round the next piece
an outburst bursts the word apart, so its letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky interruption that hampers someone giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outburst of' rearranges CHEEK into HECKE; 'cramping' puts L inside it. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt a speaker with jeers and rude remarks is an outburst of cheek that hampers them.

clue.text: It's reached by nonagenarian in Tyne, swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person reaches a milestone while swimming in the River Tyne.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagenarian is a person in their nineties, so they have reached this age.

clue.text: Man with new sign enters annually and marvels

indicators.note: enters means the man, new and sign go inside the annual abbreviation

parts.note: p.a., per annum, means annually
he stands for a man
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: A man with a new star sign comes in every year and is astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable events or wonders can be called phenomena, a plural noun like marvels.

clue.text: Plumbing system a clue to temperature briefly?

definitions.meaning: a domestic system of pipes and radiators warming a building
the central letter of the word heating is T, the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A plumber's set-up gives a hint about how warm it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the answer means the middle of HEATING, which is T, a brief form of temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler-fed network of radiators and pipes warms a whole house, a standard plumbed system.

clue.text: Serb or Schwabian's liquid intake?

explanation.walkthrough: 'intake' signals letters held within 'Serb or Schwabian's'; the whole clue also defines, since this beetroot soup is eaten across Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: This beetroot soup is a traditional Slavic and Eastern European dish, so liquid food a Serb might consume.

clue.text: US city and Tyrone town with no golf area

parts.note: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone in Northern Ireland
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American city and a Northern Irish town that has no golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyrone is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, in the United States.

clue.text: Rehearsed move's flat on stage

definitions.meaning: a planned routine from a free kick or corner in football
a flat is a piece of painted theatre scenery, a piece of the set

explanation.definitionFit: A planned play from a dead ball in sport, and also a piece of stage scenery.

clue.text: Harry had a nice big estate in Mexico

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, here roughing up the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry enjoyed a large Mexican ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb, to harass, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large landed property or ranch in Spanish-speaking America.

clue.text: Boss sorts beer crew imported

parts.note: genera are kinds or sorts in biological classification

indicators.note: imported means the crew is brought inside the beer

parts.note: lager is a type of beer
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: The boss sorts out the beer the crew has brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior executive running a business or team is its boss.

clue.text: Two studies involving minute sentence

indicators.note: involving means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to con is to study a text, and a den is a study room, so the two together give CON and DEN

clue.text: Like some bands? Endure one in English clubs

the Roman numeral I is one

clue.text: John ties up dry game

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, as is loo
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance in which numbers are drawn, like bingo.

clue.text: French queen goes over paper to have another look

parts.note: reine is French for queen
an exam paper is a test

clue.text: Varied, like laboratory scales

definitions.meaning: a varied diet is one with a healthy mix of everything
lab scales are carefully balanced and kept in good order, a literal reading

explanation.surface: Describing laboratory weighing equipment as diverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A varied mix is evenly proportioned, while precise scales are literally balanced well.

clue.text: A devotee's carrying a drink over that's picked up in Cape

clue.text: Bone Victoria found in a cell in bits

in bits means the words are broken up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Bones of someone named Victoria discovered in a prison cell, broken.

explanation.definitionFit: The collarbone is a bone joining the shoulder blade to the breastbone.

clue.text: Last appearance by Gloria — and her first!

her first letter, Gloria's initial, is G

explanation.surface: A final screen role for an actress named Gloria, which was also her debut.

clue.text: Cheap impression in paper's harbour guide?

parts.note: low prices are cheap
a watermark is a design pressed into paper during manufacture

explanation.surface: A cheap mark made in a newspaper's harbour guide.
explanation.definitionFit: The line reached by the tide at its lowest is a guide to depth for boats in a harbour.

clue.text: Not much on? Take a ride briefly in island

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its end

parts.note: to bike is to take a ride on a bicycle

clue.text: Carlisle eventually hosts record-holder

clue.text: This clue in full in Le Monde? I'd bet on it!

clue.text: Write off petrol business across the Channel

clue.text: Big swimmers gulp it while away crossing river

clue.text: It's maybe served with 5 on court in different places

clue.text: Marx brother or English golfer

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer

clue.text: Can force open bottles in their original condition
